failure_mode_downstream.value: If this roll-up is wrong the error is a MIS-GROUPED PARENT: ARNs land under the wrong service bucket. Wave 2 would then compute over a parent partition whose blocks are wrong, and the output would be a plausible per-service aggregate carrying no marker of the error. IS IT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM A GENUINE LOW-AFFINITY RESULT? PARTLY, and only by re-deriving: the parse is deterministic and total (1,689 of 1,689, 0 empties), so a mis-grouping cannot arise from missing data -- it can only arise from the ARN grammar assumption itself being wrong for some partition, e.g. a service whose ARNs place the service token elsewhere. That is checkable by re-parsing against a second ARN grammar, which THIS row does not do. Until someone does, a wrong bucket and a genuinely sparse service look identical downstream. NO FUSED VALUE IS ASSERTED HERE.
